claims.text: GDACS's event report (eventid 1029649, episode 11) assessed an Orange alert for medium humanitarian impact for a wildfire in Le Kef and Béja governorates, Tunisia, covering a 21-29 July 2026 window, citing about 11,824 hectares burned and roughly 1,224 people in the fire-affected area.

A ReliefWeb-hosted disaster/situation record titled 'TUN: Fire - 07-2026 - Tunisia Wildfires 2026' (dated 30 July 2026) exists for this event, confirming allowlisted humanitarian coverage of the Tunisia wildfires. Confirmed in a browser 2026-08-26: an IFRC situation report, originally published 30 Jul 2026 (posted 31 Jul 2026), describing a wave of fires that began on 1 June 2026 and peaked from 12 July 2026 amid an exceptional heatwave with temperatures close to 50°C in several governorates including Béja.

Re-checked 4 August 2026: GDACS's event report (eventid 1029649) still shows episode 11 (21-29 July 2026 window) as the latest, with no newer episode published and the most recent thermal-anomaly detection unchanged at 29 July 2026 — six days with no new hotspot activity. Burned area and affected population remain about 11,824 hectares and 1,224 people.

description: Wildfires broke out across Le Kef and Béja governorates in northwestern Tunisia on 21 July 2026. GDACS assessed the event at an Orange alert for medium humanitarian impact, citing about 11,824 hectares burned and roughly 1,224 people in the fire-affected area over its 21-29 July reporting window. GDACS's most recent thermal-anomaly detection remained 29 July, and after six days without new hotspot activity the fire is considered contained; no confirmed death toll has been published. A ReliefWeb disaster record, 'TUN: Fire - 07-2026 - Tunisia Wildfires 2026' (dated 30 July 2026), provides corroborating humanitarian coverage of the event.

impact.summary: GDACS assessed an Orange alert (medium humanitarian impact) for wildfires across Le Kef and Béja governorates, Tunisia, citing about 11,824 hectares burned and roughly 1,224 people in the fire-affected area over the 21-29 July 2026 window. With GDACS's most recent thermal-anomaly detection unchanged at 29 July -- six days without new hotspot activity as of 4 August -- the fire is considered contained; no confirmed death toll has been published for this fire.
